clue.text: Free from pain as seen in the old after retirement

indicators.note: something seen in another is set within it, so one piece sits inside the other
retiring means drawing back, so the word is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: YE is the archaic form of 'the', as in Ye Olde Tea Shoppe

explanation.surface: Someone finds relief from aches only once the elderly have retired.
explanation.walkthrough: The archaic 'the' comes from mock-old shop signs such as Ye Olde Inn; 'after retirement' makes it read backwards before 'seen in' takes the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone at ease is comfortable and untroubled by pain or discomfort.

clue.text: Chef's whiskers

parts.note: not a cook's moustache but the kitchen tools a cook uses to whisk eggs

explanation.definitionFit: A whisk is a hand tool for beating eggs, so a chef's whiskers are those beating gadgets.

clue.text: River getting unwholesome smell in time

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, the time letter going within the smell word

parts.note: a sour smell is a rank, unwholesome one

explanation.surface: A river picks up a nasty smell over time.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stour is the name of several English rivers, one in Kent and one in Dorset among them.

clue.text: Sniffs out the quarry, we hear, with this atomiser

indicators.note: the phrase asks the solver to listen to how words sound rather than how they are spelt

parts.note: sniffs out is scents, and the quarry is the prey

explanation.surface: A hound follows the scent of its prey, aided by a perfume spray.
explanation.walkthrough: SCENTS PREY sounds like the answer; PREY and the second word of the answer are homophones.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomiser turns perfume into a fine mist, which is exactly what a perfume sprayer does.

clue.text: Pole goes in tent to solicit

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other, the pole letter entering the tent word

parts.note: a tent is made of canvas, and camping is 'under canvas'
S stands for the South Pole

explanation.surface: Putting up a tent: the pole is pushed inside the canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: To canvass is to go round asking for votes or orders, to solicit support.

clue.text: it's noon madness brings on such ideas

indicators.note: madness suggests disorder, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: Midday madness puts strange ideas in one's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Notions and ideas are both thoughts or beliefs held in the mind.

clue.text: Sinned, in a surplice

definitions.meaning: took something unlawfully, a theft being a sin
a clerical vestment, the scarf-like band a priest wears over a surplice

explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of steal for one sense; for the other, the long liturgical scarf a priest wears with vestments.

clue.text: Trouble caused by a revolting beast

parts.note: one who revolts against authority is a rebel
a lion is a large wild beast

explanation.surface: Unrest is stirred up by a disgusting animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' looks like 'disgusting' but means 'rising in revolt'.
explanation.definitionFit: Civil trouble or unrest can take the form of an uprising against those in power.

clue.text: It turns up, following you? Unlikely!

definitions.text: It turns up, following you? Unlikely!

indicators.note: one piece comes after the other in the answer

parts.note: YE is the archaic plural of you

indicators.note: in a down answer turning up means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

explanation.surface: Is the abominable snowman tracking you? Hardly likely!
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: the creature supposedly trails walkers, and 'Unlikely!' is a sceptic's verdict on its existence.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan snowman, a creature said to leave tracks behind travellers, whose existence is unlikely.

clue.text: When captured, isn't charged

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'When captured, isn't charged' (8) for INTEREST: no parse makes sense of 'isn't'; probably an OCR or print error, not found online

clue.text: Tuber with almost entirely circular fruit

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Tuber with almost entirely circular fruit' (6-3) for GROUNDNUT: no wordplay gives the opening G; likely garbled in OCR, not found online
annotationWithheld.clue: Tuber with almost entirely circular fruit

clue.text: Path or part of one

parts.note: taken as written
a bit is a small part of something

explanation.surface: A route described as a path, or a section of one.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbit is the curved course a planet or satellite follows around a body.

clue.text: Headless beer — that is uncanny

indicators.note: without its head means the first letter is lost

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Flat beer with no foam on top: how strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headless' drops the B of BEER to leave EER; a headless beer also suggests one with no froth.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eerie is weird and unsettling, strange in a spooky way.

clue.text: Especially on top

definitions.meaning: most importantly, more than anything else

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both 'most of all' and literally 'higher than everything'.

clue.text: Go and resign as distressed by hostile behaviour

indicators.note: distressed suggests being thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Being told to go and resign makes someone upset at the hostility shown.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostile, attacking conduct is what aggression means.

clue.text: information dispensers, in banks?

parts.note: people who tell things dispense information; the bank staff at the counter, who dispense cash, share their title

explanation.definitionFit: Those who tell are tellers, and a bank clerk serving customers is called a teller.

clue.text: Tend to leap first?

definitions.meaning: to care for or mind someone
the proverb says look before you leap; leaping first means the looking comes later

explanation.definitionFit: To tend someone is to care for them; read literally, the phrase puts the looking later than the leap.

clue.text: Burning though there's water round

parts.note: the sea is a body of water
a ring is a round shape

explanation.surface: Scorching heat even though water surrounds us.
explanation.definitionFit: Searing heat is burning, scorching heat.

clue.text: First class leader savaged by terrier

parts.note: A1 means first class, with the 1 as I

indicators.note: savaged suggests being mauled out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A top-class pack leader is mauled by a terrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' looks like the pack's head, but 'savaged' tells you to rearrange it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Airedale is a large breed of terrier from Yorkshire.

clue.text: Duck in the list, with fowl

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other, the duck letter within the list word

parts.note: a roster is a list of names on duty
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A duck is put on the list along with the other poultry.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooster is a cock, a male domestic fowl.

clue.text: Go back to find right way out

parts.note: an egress is an exit

explanation.surface: Retracing one's steps to find the correct exit.
explanation.definitionFit: To regress is to return to an earlier state, to revert.

clue.text: Ancient poetic figure

parts.note: the old sailor of Coleridge's Rime, called Ancient in the title

explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge's poem is the Rime of the Ancient Mariner, so its seafaring hero is an ancient poetic figure.

clue.text: For the small amount held by mother, detectives ring up

indicators.note: one piece is gripped within the other, the reversed letters inside the mother word

parts.note: mum is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: in a down answer up means the letters read upwards, reversed

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: Detectives phone for a little information held by someone's mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns CIDO into ODIC, which 'held by' places inside MUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A modicum is a small quantity, a little bit.

clue.text: Saved and gave lads treat

indicators.note: to treat is to process or handle, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone was thrifty and gave the boys a treat.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvaged means rescued from loss or wreck, saved.

clue.text: Move out-no love lost, in spite

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order
lost means the named letter is taken away

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, so O

explanation.surface: Get out: there is no love left, in spite of everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' takes O (love) from NO to leave N; 'out' rearranges MOVE plus N.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom is malice or bitter spite in words or manner.

clue.text: Judges writing to banker

indicators.note: to means added to, so the writing letters follow the banker

parts.note: a river has banks, so a banker is a river; the Dee is one
MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Magistrates write a letter to their bank manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is crossword slang for a river, a thing with banks.
explanation.definitionFit: To deem is to judge or consider something to be so.

clue.text: Lacks occupation

parts.note: reads like a jobless person, but describes a place with no occupants

explanation.definitionFit: Something vacant has nobody in it, so it has no occupants.

clue.text: Stuff surfacing in wine refuse

indicators.note: in a down answer, surfacing means coming up, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: to stuff is to cram

explanation.surface: Debris floats up in the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc is the residue of grape skins and pips left after pressing in winemaking.

clue.text: Keep performance running in London

parts.note: an act is a performance on stage
on means running, as a show that is on

explanation.surface: A show is kept going in a London theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' is padding for the surface; the definition is a place in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Acton is a district of west London.

clue.text: Point to a cut lip and hear why treatment produces blue gums

parts.note: E is a compass point, east

indicators.note: treatment suggests working on something, so the letters are rearranged
hear signals that a word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the word why sounds like the letter Y

explanation.surface: Instructions to treat a cut lip using gum-tree products.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hear' turns the word why into a single letter, which joins the cut lip in the 'treatment' mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue gums are Australian trees of the genus whose plural this is.

clue.text: Has a place in cell with companion and room contrived for several more

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

indicators.note: contrived means made up artfully, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: some more means several more, giving the word for several

explanation.surface: A friend shares a room arranged for more people.
explanation.definitionFit: A chromosome is a thread-like structure in the nucleus of a living cell carrying genes.

clue.text: Praise not intended for the girl, it's said

indicators.note: it's said signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: meant not for her but for the male, the word him

explanation.surface: A compliment is meant for him, not for her, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymn is a song of praise to God.
